title: Our Fridays
story_note: A fictional story written by the author about friendship, unspoken love and change. No real person is depicted or voiced.
audience: Young Ethiopian adults (the author's friends and cohort colleagues), watching on a phone.
intent: They recognise the feeling of something left unsaid, and leave warmed that the friendship continues.
narration_style: One warm, reflective narrator, natural pacing. Quoted dialogue is read by the narrator.
visual_style: Naturalistic cinematic photography in a contemporary Ethiopian city; muted terracotta, coffee brown and navy palette; gentle natural light; restrained expressions; shallow depth of field. Keep the subject central and allow reframing for both portrait and landscape. No generated legible text, logos, watermarks or celebrity likenesses.
style_block: Naturalistic cinematic photograph, contemporary Ethiopian city, muted terracotta, coffee brown and navy palette, gentle natural light, shallow depth of field, restrained expressions, subject centred, no text, no logos, no watermark.

characters.name: Rahel
characters.description: Fictional Ethiopian woman in her late twenties, warm brown skin, shoulder-length dark curly hair, thoughtful expressive eyes.
characters.wardrobe: Cream knit top, olive jacket and a simple tan shoulder bag.

characters.name: Bekele
characters.description: Fictional Ethiopian man in his late twenties, warm brown skin, close-cropped curly dark hair, short neat beard, gentle and reserved expression.
characters.wardrobe: Navy overshirt over a light grey shirt, dark trousers and a modest wristwatch.

music.caption: Understated solo piano with a soft warm ambient pad, intimate, reflective, slow, sparse, no lead melody competing with a voice, instrumental, no vocals.
music.mix_direction: Lower the music under narration; confirm levels by listening after generation.

cues.direction: Piano enters softly; warm and familiar.
Thins to pad and single notes; night, hesitation.
Opening figure returns and resolves into the end card.

narration.text: Every Friday, Rahel and Bekele met at the same small café. She knew exactly how he took his coffee.
narration.source_en: Every Friday, Rahel and Bekele met at the same small café. She knew exactly how he took his coffee.
narration.subtitle_en: Every Friday, Rahel and Bekele met at the same small café. She knew exactly how he took his coffee.

shots.keyframe_prompt: Inside a small café at golden hour, Rahel and Bekele sit close together at a wooden table with two simple cups. Rahel slides his preferred coffee toward Bekele. Frame them together in the centre with enough headroom for a portrait crop.
shots.motion_prompt: A gentle slow push toward the table as Rahel slides a cup toward Bekele.

shots.reason: Show his attention and introduce his unspoken feelings.

narration.text: He knew when her smile was hiding a difficult day. What she didn’t know was that he loved her.
narration.source_en: He knew when her smile was hiding a difficult day. What she didn’t know was that he loved her.
narration.subtitle_en: He knew when her smile was hiding a difficult day. What she didn’t know was that he loved her.

shots.keyframe_prompt: At the same café table, Rahel gives a small tired smile; Bekele notices with a quiet sympathetic look and gently moves her cup closer. The mood is intimate, restrained and clearly platonic from her point of view.
shots.motion_prompt: Subtle eye movement and a small movement of Bekele's hand toward the coffee cup.

shots.reason: Introduce the change that puts their friendship under pressure.

narration.text: One afternoon, Rahel told him she’d accepted a job in another city. Bekele smiled and told her he was proud.
narration.source_en: One afternoon, Rahel told him she’d accepted a job in another city. Bekele smiled and told her he was proud.
narration.subtitle_en: One afternoon, Rahel told him she’d accepted a job in another city. Bekele smiled and told her he was proud.

shots.keyframe_prompt: In the same café Rahel shares good news with a mixture of excitement and nervousness; Bekele responds with a supportive smile that hides a trace of sadness. Focus on their faces and body language rather than phone text.
shots.motion_prompt: Rahel speaks with a small excited gesture; Bekele smiles gently.

narration.text: That night, he typed, “There’s something I’ve wanted to tell you.” His thumb hovered over send.
narration.source_en: That night, he typed, “There’s something I’ve wanted to tell you.” His thumb hovered over send.
narration.subtitle_en: That night, he typed, “There’s something I’ve wanted to tell you.” His thumb hovered over send.

shots.keyframe_prompt: In Bekele's modest apartment at night, he sits alone holding a phone, lit softly by a lamp and the screen. Frame his face and hand; the screen remains blank for text to be added in editing.
shots.motion_prompt: Slow close-in toward the phone as Bekele's thumb pauses above the screen.

overlay_text.text: There’s something I’ve wanted to tell you.

shots.reason: Show the cost of his hesitation.

narration.text: But he deleted the message. He was afraid the truth might change their friendship.
narration.source_en: But he deleted the message. He was afraid the truth might change their friendship.
narration.subtitle_en: But he deleted the message. He was afraid the truth might change their friendship.

shots.keyframe_prompt: A close view of Bekele looking between his phone and a small, unbranded printed photograph of two friends at a café. His expression is conflicted; the phone screen is neutral and blank.
shots.motion_prompt: He lowers his gaze and slowly withdraws his thumb, leaving a beat of stillness.

shots.reason: Let Rahel express her own feelings while showing Bekele's care.

narration.text: At the bus station, Rahel admitted she was scared. Bekele picked up her bag and walked beside her.
narration.source_en: At the bus station, Rahel admitted she was scared. Bekele picked up her bag and walked beside her.
narration.subtitle_en: At the bus station, Rahel admitted she was scared. Bekele picked up her bag and walked beside her.

shots.keyframe_prompt: At a contemporary city bus station during soft morning light, Rahel with her tan shoulder bag looks nervous before a departure. Bekele lifts a single travel bag and walks beside her; both are grouped in the central crop-safe area.
shots.motion_prompt: Bekele picks up the bag as Rahel takes a small breath; they take a few gentle steps.

shots.reason: Show her active choice to keep their friendship alive.

narration.text: Before boarding, she handed him a small packet of coffee. “So we can still have our Fridays,” she said.
narration.source_en: Before boarding, she handed him a small packet of coffee. “So we can still have our Fridays,” she said.
narration.subtitle_en: Before boarding, she handed him a small packet of coffee. “So we can still have our Fridays,” she said.

shots.keyframe_prompt: At the bus station Rahel offers Bekele a plain unbranded small paper packet of coffee beans. Their hands and warm, restrained expressions are visible. A bus stands softly out of focus behind them.
shots.motion_prompt: Rahel extends the coffee packet; Bekele accepts it and they exchange a quiet smile.

shots.reason: Resolve the separation with a promise of continued friendship while leaving his feelings unspoken.

narration.text: As the bus pulled away, his phone lit up: “Friday. Same time?” Bekele smiled and typed, “I’ll be there.”
narration.source_en: As the bus pulled away, his phone lit up: “Friday. Same time?” Bekele smiled and typed, “I’ll be there.”
narration.subtitle_en: As the bus pulled away, his phone lit up: “Friday. Same time?” Bekele smiled and typed, “I’ll be there.”

shots.keyframe_prompt: Bekele stands at the bus station holding the coffee packet; a departing bus is softly blurred in the background. He glances at his phone and smiles gently; keep the screen blank for the message to be added in editing.
shots.motion_prompt: The bus moves gently out of frame as Bekele lowers his gaze to the phone and smiles.

production_notes: All times are planned. Record and measure narration before locking timing.
Character descriptions and Ethiopian setting are editable suggestions, not depictions of real people.
Create and approve character reference images before keyframes; none are included yet.
Subtitles must be timed from final speech and rendered with readable line lengths and safe margins in each aspect ratio.
Add phone messages and end-card text programmatically rather than relying on generated text.
Portrait and landscape compositions must be checked independently; some shots may need separate reframing.
No film, model output, audience test, experiment or model-call log is included in this starter.
